scenarios.hypothesis: A message or cached response authorized in session generation N remains accepted after reconnect creates session generation N+1 without rebinding the logical operation.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock loopback endpoint and read-only synthetic consumer emit only a generation-tagged inert receipt when the deliberately stale session message is accepted.
scenarios.positive_control: The same synthetic operation sent under the current session generation N+1 is accepted once and produces the expected read-only receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: The identical payload carrying an unrelated synthetic peer identity is rejected before the mock downstream consumer can record any semantic action.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled external traffic, or cannot remain synthetic and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding message and response correlation to the current session generation, the stale N message is rejected while the N+1 positive control succeeds.
scenarios.peer_session_role_generation: Record synthetic peer identity, stable role generation, connection generations before and after reconnect, old session N, new session N+1, and stream generation.
scenarios.transition_guard_authenticated_context: Bind the stale message to its transition identity, guard, authenticated principal, authorization context, and prove the guard consumed old session authority after reconnect.
scenarios.replay_retry_idempotency_state: Record logical operation identity, repeated message ID, replay classification, idempotency generation, response-cache generation, and whether the message is treated as old or current.
scenarios.timeout_cancel_reset_reconnect_state: Record the reconnect generation, closure or reset of connection N, creation of connection/session N+1, and the exact revocation point expected for N authority.
scenarios.commit_terminal_downstream_action: Separate stale message acceptance, transition acceptance, acknowledgment, any semantic commit, final inert downstream action, terminal state, and cleanup completion.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the exact mock read-only consumer method that accepts the stale generation and emits the structured synthetic receipt for the controlled operation.
scenarios.effective_protocol_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to acceptance of one synthetic protocol operation under a stale session generation after controlled reconnect.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one inert structured receipt containing peer, old/new session generations, message identity, and no external or persistent effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate peer identity, connection generation, old session, new session, message generation, transition, consumer, and inert receipt in one deterministic record.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold peer, payload, message ID, protocol state, and consumer constant while changing only stale session N to current session N+1 and compare acceptance.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject documented reconnect continuity, harness ID reuse, ambiguous response correlation, positive-control output, or a different logical operation as explanations.
scenarios.evidence_level: PST3 because a read-only mock consumer accepts a synthetic message under the wrong session generation after reconnect in a deterministic fixture.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: PST3 maximum until a bounded protocol effect plus complete lifecycle, correlation, counterfactual, receipt, and remediation evidence justify PST4 or PST5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A retry of one logical synthetic operation crosses the semantic commit point twice because duplicate suppression is keyed to request generation rather than operation identity.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled fake transaction ledger records only inert synthetic commit markers and effect counts; no real payment, file, account, or external resource is touched.
scenarios.positive_control: One synthetic operation with one attempt produces exactly one fake-ledger commit and one deterministic read-only result receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: Two distinct logical operations with distinct idempotency identities each produce one commit, proving the ledger and duplicate detector can distinguish intended separate effects.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled external traffic, or cannot remain synthetic and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding idempotency to logical operation plus current session/transaction generation, the retry yields one commit while two distinct operations still yield two.
scenarios.peer_session_role_generation: Keep peer, role, connection, session, stream, and transaction generations explicit and constant across first attempt and retry so duplication is isolated.
scenarios.transition_guard_authenticated_context: Capture the commit transition guard, authenticated context, authorization context, and show both retry attempts satisfy the same current protocol authority.
scenarios.replay_retry_idempotency_state: Bind logical operation identity, first and second request IDs, retry attempts, idempotency key, duplicate-suppression generation, response cache, and effect count.
scenarios.timeout_cancel_reset_reconnect_state: Record that no timeout, cancellation, reset, or reconnect occurs in this case so duplicate commit cannot be attributed to lifecycle replacement.
scenarios.commit_terminal_downstream_action: Trace request acceptance, acknowledgment, first semantic commit, retry acceptance, second semantic commit, fake-ledger markers, terminal state, and cleanup.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the fake ledger commit consumer that increments the bounded synthetic effect count and emits deterministic commit receipts for both attempts.
scenarios.effective_protocol_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to duplicating one inert synthetic semantic commit for the same logical operation under a controlled retry sequence.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a fake-ledger count of two inert markers for one logical operation, with no external transfer or persistent production effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind both attempt generations, shared logical operation identity, idempotency state, commit generations, effect count, and ledger receipts deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold operation, peer, session, transaction, payload, and retry sequence fixed while changing only generation-blind to operation-bound idempotency handling.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject intentional at-least-once commit semantics, two distinct logical operations, positive-control duplication, response-cache artifacts, or concurrency-only causes.
scenarios.evidence_level: PST4 because a bounded duplicate inert commit is causally tied to the exact retry, idempotency, protocol-state, and commit tuple.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: PST4 maximum until complete operation provenance, alternative elimination, counterfactuals, receipt binding, and remediation replay satisfy PST5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic operation authorized while the peer has role generation N remains consumable after an authoritative role change advances the peer to generation N+1.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock read-only privileged consumer returns only an inert synthetic authorization marker showing which role generation it accepted, with no real privileged action.
scenarios.positive_control: The same operation under a current role generation that is explicitly permitted by the synthetic policy produces the expected inert authorization marker.
scenarios.negative_control: A fresh operation initiated after the role downgrade under generation N+1 is rejected by the same transition guard and produces no privileged marker.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled external traffic, or cannot remain synthetic and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After rebinding pending operations to current role generation at transition or commit time, stale N authority is rejected while authorized current-role controls pass.
scenarios.peer_session_role_generation: Record peer identity, authenticated principal, stable session generation, old role generation N, new role generation N+1, and operation generation.
scenarios.transition_guard_authenticated_context: Bind initial authorization and later transition/commit guard to authenticated context, authorization context, and show stale role generation N is reused after change.
scenarios.replay_retry_idempotency_state: Record that the operation is not a retry or replay, while preserving message and operation identities so stale role authority is isolated from duplicate semantics.
scenarios.timeout_cancel_reset_reconnect_state: Record that no reconnect or timeout is necessary; the authoritative role-generation transition alone is the lifecycle boundary under test.
scenarios.commit_terminal_downstream_action: Separate initial authorization, role change, later transition acceptance, inert downstream privileged marker, semantic commit state, terminal state, and cleanup.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the exact mock read-only privileged consumer that interprets the stale role-bound operation and emits the inert synthetic marker.
scenarios.effective_protocol_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to one synthetic role-gated protocol action remaining accepted after the authoritative role generation changed.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one read-only authorization receipt containing old/current role generations and no external, destructive, or persistent privileged effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate peer, session, role N authorization, role N+1 state, operation generation, final guard, consumer identity, and inert receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold session, message, operation, transition, and consumer constant while changing only current role generation from stale N binding to revalidated N+1.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject advisory-only role semantics, delayed policy propagation permitted by contract, stale logs, different sessions, or a separate authorization-boundary cause.
scenarios.evidence_level: PST3 because an inert downstream consumer accepts a synthetic protocol action using stale role generation after an authoritative role change.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: PST3 maximum until a stronger bounded protocol effect and complete role, transition, alternative, receipt, and remediation evidence justify promotion.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic operation times out or is cancelled in generation N, then its late completion is routed into a replacement transaction or session generation N+1.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled mock completion router and read-only consumer emit only an inert generation-tagged completion receipt without external state or production side effects.
scenarios.positive_control: A completion arriving before timeout for the current operation generation is routed to the intended synthetic transaction and produces one expected receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A late completion carrying an unrelated operation identity is rejected before the replacement transaction or downstream consumer accepts it.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled external traffic, or cannot remain synthetic and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After fencing completion routing by operation and lifecycle generation, the old N completion is rejected while the current N+1 operation completes normally.
scenarios.peer_session_role_generation: Record synthetic peer and role, session generation, old transaction/stream generation N, replacement generation N+1, and their operation identities.
scenarios.transition_guard_authenticated_context: Capture completion transition guard, authenticated session context, ownership check, and show the stale completion passes despite old operation generation.
scenarios.replay_retry_idempotency_state: Record whether the replacement operation reuses request IDs or idempotency state and prove the stale completion is not merely a legitimate retry response.
scenarios.timeout_cancel_reset_reconnect_state: Bind timeout generation, cancellation request and acknowledgement, old terminal state, replacement transaction creation, and late completion generation.
scenarios.commit_terminal_downstream_action: Trace timeout/cancel transition, old terminal state, late completion acceptance, replacement transaction mutation, inert downstream receipt, and cleanup state.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the mock read-only completion consumer that receives the old generation result under the replacement transaction and records the mismatch.
scenarios.effective_protocol_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to stale synthetic completion acceptance across a controlled timeout/cancellation generation boundary.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one inert completion receipt naming old and replacement generations; no real transaction, file, network, or account state is modified.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate old operation, timeout/cancel generation, replacement transaction, late completion identity, routing decision, consumer, and receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold payload, peer, consumer, and replacement transaction fixed while changing only completion generation binding from old N to current N+1.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject explicitly non-cancelling timeout semantics, completion for a different operation, request-ID collision by harness, reconnect continuity, or pure scheduling race.
scenarios.evidence_level: PST3 because the mock downstream consumer accepts a stale completion under the wrong transaction or session generation after timeout/cancellation.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: PST3 maximum until a bounded protocol effect and complete timeout, routing, counterfactual, receipt, and remediation proof support a higher level.
